paragraphs.text: וְהָ֣אָדָ֔ם יָדַ֖ע אֶת־חַוָּ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וַתַּ֙הַר֙ וַתֵּ֣לֶד אֶת־קַ֔יִן וַתֹּ֕אמֶר קָנִ֥יתִי אִ֖ישׁ אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: The human knew his woman Chavvah, and she conceived and bore Cain. She said, "I have made a man — YHWH himself!"
i18n.he: וְהָ֣אָדָ֔ם יָדַ֖ע אֶת־חַוָּ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וַתַּ֙הַר֙ וַתֵּ֣לֶד אֶת־קַ֔יִן וַתֹּ֕אמֶר קָנִ֥יתִי אִ֖ישׁ אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃
i18n.de: Der Mensch erkannte seine Frau Chawwa, und sie empfing und gebar Kajin. Sie sprach: "Ich habe einen Mann gewonnen — YHWH selbst!"
i18n.es: El ser humano conoció a su mujer Chavvah, y ella concibió y dio a luz a Caín. Y dijo: «He adquirido un varón con YHWH mismo».
i18n.fr: L'être humain connut Chavvah sa femme, et elle conçut et enfanta Caïn. Elle dit : « J'ai acquis un homme avec YHWH ! »
i18n.ja: 人はその女ハヴァを知り、彼女は身ごもってカインを産んだ。彼女は言った、「私はYHWHと共に男を得た」。
i18n.ko: 사람이 자기 여자 하와를 알았고, 그녀가 잉태하여 카인을 낳았다. 그녀가 말하였다, "내가 YHWH로 사람을 얻었다!"
i18n.ru: И человек познал жену свою Хавву, и она зачала и родила Каина. И сказала она: «Приобрела я человека с YHWH!»
i18n.zh: 那人与他的女人夏娃同房；她怀孕，生了该隐。她说：「我藉 YHWH 得了一个男子！」
i18n.zh-Hant: 那人認識了他的女人哈娃，她懷孕生了該隱。她說：「我藉 YHWH 得了一個男子！」

notes.official:
**A startling birth-saying.** The verse ends with one of the strangest constructions in Genesis: קָנִיתִי אִישׁ אֶת־יְהוָה qaniti ish et-YHWH. The verb קָנָה qana spans 'acquire, get, possess' and 'create, beget' (used of divine creation in 14:19, Ps 139:13). אֶת־יְהוָה et-YHWH is the direct-object marker followed by the Tetragrammaton — read straight, this means 'I have created/acquired a man, YHWH' (with YHWH in apposition to *a man*).

Most translations supply a preposition that isn't there. KJV: 'I have gotten a man *from* the LORD'. NJPS: 'I have gained a male child *with the help of* the LORD'. Alter: 'I have got me a man *with* the LORD'. The Hebrew has only the direct-object marker — no 'from', no 'with', no 'help of'.

Reading the Hebrew straight yields a Chavvah who frames her firstborn in unmistakably divine-creative language. The first human birth outside the garden is described with the same verb used elsewhere for the Elohim's making of the cosmos. Whether *et-YHWH* is appositional ('a man — YHWH', the strongest reading), associative ('a man, with YHWH'), or instrumental ('a man, via YHWH'), the Hebrew leaves un-decided. WoH takes the strong reading — the saying claims an unmistakably divine-creative scale for the act of birth — and lets commentary surface the softer alternatives.

Note that Chavvah here invokes *YHWH*, not *Elohim* or *YHWH-Elohim*. The personal name has come fully forward in her speech; by v25 she will shift back to *Elohim*.

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֣סֶף לָלֶ֔דֶת אֶת־אָחִ֖יו אֶת־הָ֑בֶל וַֽיְהִי־הֶ֙בֶל֙ רֹ֣עֵה צֹ֔אן וְקַ֕יִן הָיָ֖ה עֹבֵ֥ד אֲדָמָֽה׃

i18n.en: She bore again — his brother Hevel. Hevel became a shepherd of flock, and Cain became a worker of the ground.
i18n.he: וַתֹּ֣סֶף לָלֶ֔דֶת אֶת־אָחִ֖יו אֶת־הָ֑בֶל וַֽיְהִי־הֶ֙בֶל֙ רֹ֣עֵה צֹ֔אן וְקַ֕יִן הָיָ֖ה עֹבֵ֥ד אֲדָמָֽה׃
i18n.de: Sie gebar wiederum — seinen Bruder Hewel. Hewel wurde ein Hirte der Herde, und Kajin wurde ein Bearbeiter des Ackerbodens.
i18n.es: Dio a luz otra vez—a su hermano Hevel. Hevel llegó a ser pastor de ovejas, y Caín llegó a ser labrador del suelo.
i18n.fr: Elle enfanta encore — son frère Hével. Hével devint berger de petit bétail, et Caïn devint cultivateur du sol.
i18n.ja: 彼女はまた産んだ——その弟ヘヴェルを。ヘヴェルは群れを飼う者となり、カインは大地を耕す者となった。
i18n.ko: 그녀가 다시 낳았으니 — 그의 아우 헤벨이다. 헤벨은 양 떼를 치는 자가 되었고, 카인은 땅을 일구는 자가 되었다.
i18n.ru: И снова родила—брата его Хевеля. И стал Хевель пастухом овец, а Каин стал возделывателем земли.
i18n.zh: 她又生了他的兄弟亚伯。亚伯成了牧羊的人，该隐则成了耕作可耕之地的人。
i18n.zh-Hant: 她又再生了—該隱的兄弟亞伯。亞伯成了牧羊的，該隱成了耕作土壤的。

notes.official:
**The second son arrives in silence.** Where Cain's birth was crowned by Chavvah's elaborate etymology (v1), Hevel's birth is given in five Hebrew words with no naming-speech, no etymology, no comment. He is *his brother* before he is named. The name itself — הֶבֶל hevel — is the word that opens Qohelet ('vapor of vapors, all is vapor'). It denotes breath, mist, fleetingness, futility. The text gives him no naming-ceremony because the name *is* the foreshadowing.

The brothers split the post-garden economic order between them: עֹבֵד אֲדָמָה oved adamah (worker of the ground) for Cain, רֹעֵה צֹאן roeh tzon (shepherd of flock) for Hevel. Cain inherits the human-and-ground bond from 2:15, 3:23 — same verb עָבַד avad. Hevel takes up the pastoral counterpart. ANE life's two foundational economies — settled agriculture and nomadic pastoralism — stand side by side, in two brothers.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיְהִ֖י מִקֵּ֣ץ יָמִ֑ים וַיָּבֵ֨א קַ֜יִן מִפְּרִ֧י הָֽאֲדָמָ֛ה מִנְחָ֖ה לַֽיהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: After some time, Cain brought from the fruit of the ground an offering to YHWH.
i18n.he: וַֽיְהִ֖י מִקֵּ֣ץ יָמִ֑ים וַיָּבֵ֨א קַ֜יִן מִפְּרִ֧י הָֽאֲדָמָ֛ה מִנְחָ֖ה לַֽיהוָֽה׃
i18n.de: Nach einiger Zeit brachte Kajin von der Frucht des Ackerbodens eine Opfergabe für YHWH.
i18n.es: Pasado algún tiempo, Caín trajo del fruto del suelo una ofrenda a YHWH.
i18n.fr: Au bout de quelque temps, Caïn apporta du fruit du sol une offrande à YHWH.
i18n.ja: ある時の後、カインは大地の実りからの供え物をYHWHのもとへ携えてきた。
i18n.ko: 얼마 후, 카인이 땅의 열매에서 YHWH께 제물을 가져왔다.
i18n.ru: По прошествии времени принёс Каин от плодов земли приношение YHWH.
i18n.zh: 过了一段日子，该隐从可耕之地的出产中拿来献给 YHWH 为供物。
i18n.zh-Hant: 過了些時候，該隱從土壤的出產中拿來作為祭物獻給 YHWH。

notes.official: *Minchah* — **an offering**. The word is the general term for a presented gift or tribute (it will later specialize to the grain-offering of the priestly system, Lev 2). Cain, the worker of the ground, brings what the ground yields: *from the fruit of the ground*. The description is unmarked — no mention of quality, firstness, or selection — and the verse sets up the contrast with v4 without yet drawing a verdict. The text's silence about *why* one offering is regarded is the point v5 will insist on.

paragraphs.text: וְהֶ֨בֶל הֵבִ֥יא גַם־ה֛וּא מִבְּכֹר֥וֹת צֹאנ֖וֹ וּמֵֽחֶלְבֵהֶ֑ן וַיִּ֣שַׁע יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־הֶ֖בֶל וְאֶל־מִנְחָתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And Hevel also brought — from the firstborn of his flock, and from their fat portions. YHWH looked favorably on Hevel and on his offering;
i18n.he: וְהֶ֨בֶל הֵבִ֥יא גַם־ה֛וּא מִבְּכֹר֥וֹת צֹאנ֖וֹ וּמֵֽחֶלְבֵהֶ֑ן וַיִּ֣שַׁע יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־הֶ֖בֶל וְאֶל־מִנְחָתֽוֹ׃
i18n.de: Und auch Hewel brachte — von den Erstgeborenen seiner Herde und von ihren Fettstücken. YHWH blickte gnädig auf Hewel und auf seine Opfergabe;
i18n.es: Y Hevel también trajo—de los primogénitos de su rebaño, y de sus porciones de grasa. YHWH miró favorablemente a Hevel y a su ofrenda;
i18n.fr: Et Hével aussi apporta — des premiers-nés de son troupeau et de leurs parts grasses. YHWH regarda avec faveur Hével et son offrande ;
i18n.ja: ヘヴェルもまた——その群れの初子と、その脂の部分から携えてきた。YHWHはヘヴェルとその供え物に目を留められた。
i18n.ko: 헤벨도 가져왔으니 — 자기 양 떼의 첫배 새끼와 그 기름진 부분에서 가져왔다. YHWH께서는 헤벨과 그의 제물을 호의로 보셨다;
i18n.ru: И Хевель также принёс—от первородных стада своего и от тука их. И призрел YHWH благосклонно на Хевеля и на приношение его;
i18n.zh: 亚伯也献上——是他羊群中头生的，以及它们脂油的部分。YHWH 悦纳亚伯及他的供物；
i18n.zh-Hant: 亞伯也獻上了—從他羊群中頭生的，並牠們的脂肪。YHWH 悅納了亞伯與他的祭物；

notes.official: Hevel's offering is described with two markers Cain's lacked: the **firstborn** of his flock (*bekhorot*) and their **fat portions** (*chelev*) — the firstlings and the choicest part, the fat later reserved as the deity's own portion (Lev 3:16). Where Cain brought produce, Hevel brought the best of it. *Vayisha* — from שָׁעָה *shaah*, "to gaze at, regard, pay heed to" — YHWH *looked* upon Hevel and his gift. The narrative sets the selectivity beside the regard but pointedly refuses to weld them into cause and effect; the reader is left to notice a contrast the text declines to name (see v5).

paragraphs.text: וְאֶל־קַ֥יִן וְאֶל־מִנְחָת֖וֹ לֹ֣א שָׁעָ֑ה וַיִּ֤חַר לְקַ֙יִן֙ מְאֹ֔ד וַֽיִּפְּל֖וּ פָּנָֽיו׃

i18n.en: but on Cain and on his offering he did not look favorably. Cain burned greatly, and his face fell.
i18n.he: וְאֶל־קַ֥יִן וְאֶל־מִנְחָת֖וֹ לֹ֣א שָׁעָ֑ה וַיִּ֤חַר לְקַ֙יִן֙ מְאֹ֔ד וַֽיִּפְּל֖וּ פָּנָֽיו׃
i18n.de: aber auf Kajin und auf seine Opfergabe blickte er nicht gnädig. Kajin entbrannte sehr, und sein Angesicht fiel.
i18n.es: pero a Caín y a su ofrenda no miró favorablemente. Y Caín ardió grandemente, y decayó su rostro.
i18n.fr: mais Caïn et son offrande, il ne les regarda pas avec faveur. Caïn brûla violemment, et son visage tomba.
i18n.ja: しかしカインとその供え物には目を留められなかった。カインは激しく燃え、その顔は伏せた。
i18n.ko: 그러나 카인과 그의 제물은 호의로 보지 않으셨다. 카인은 크게 분노하였고, 그의 얼굴이 떨어졌다.
i18n.ru: а на Каина и на приношение его не призрел благосклонно. И сильно разгорелся Каин, и поникло лицо его.
i18n.zh: 却不悦纳该隐及他的供物。该隐就大大恼怒，脸色沉了下来。
i18n.zh-Hant: 但對該隱與他的祭物，祂卻不悅納。該隱大大發怒，臉色變了。

notes.official:
**The text gives no reason.** YHWH regards one offering and not the other; no verse explains why. Tradition fills the gap: the rabbinic and patristic readings note that Hevel brought *firstborn* and *fat portions* — the choicest parts — while Cain's offering is described only as 'from the fruit of the ground' with no equivalent superlatives. Whether this carries the explanatory weight tradition gives it is debated. The Hebrew's silence is conspicuous: the differential is data, not justified outcome.

The asymmetry generates the chapter. Note that the *response* to the differential is what is judged — not the offering itself, not the differential. YHWH's next speech (vv. 6–7) addresses Cain's *anger*, not his offering, and offers a path forward (*if you do well, lifting; if not, sin couches*). The differential is the setup; what Cain does with it is the trial.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־קָ֑יִן לָ֚מָּה חָ֣רָה לָ֔ךְ וְלָ֖מָּה נָפְל֥וּ פָנֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: YHWH said to Cain, "Why have you burned, and why has your face fallen?
i18n.he: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־קָ֑יִן לָ֚מָּה חָ֣רָה לָ֔ךְ וְלָ֖מָּה נָפְל֥וּ פָנֶֽיךָ׃
i18n.de: YHWH sprach zu Kajin: "Warum bist du entbrannt, und warum ist dein Angesicht gefallen?
i18n.es: YHWH dijo a Caín: «¿Por qué has ardido, y por qué ha decaído tu rostro?
i18n.fr: YHWH dit à Caïn : « Pourquoi as-tu brûlé, et pourquoi ton visage est-il tombé ?
i18n.ja: YHWHはカインに言った、「なぜお前は燃え、なぜお前の顔は伏せたのか。
i18n.ko: YHWH께서 카인에게 말씀하셨다, "어찌하여 너는 분노하였으며, 어찌하여 너의 얼굴이 떨어졌느냐?
i18n.ru: И сказал YHWH Каину: «Почему ты разгорелся, и почему поникло лицо твоё?
i18n.zh: YHWH 对该隐说：「你为什么恼怒？为什么脸色沉下来？
i18n.zh-Hant: YHWH 對該隱說：「你為何發怒？你的臉色為何變了？

notes.official: The divine question comes *before* the deed, not after. Where 3:9 and v9 below interrogate a transgression already committed, here YHWH addresses Cain in the gap between the fallen face and the raised hand — *why has your face fallen?* — turning the moment into an offered choice rather than a verdict. The mercy of the scene is its timing: Cain is met while the act is still only anger, and v7 will lay out the fork in front of him.

i18n.en: Is it not so: if you do well, lifting; and if you do not do well, sin couches at the door — and its longing is for you, but you shall rule over it."

notes.official:
**Two grammatical features and one cross-textual parallel.**

First, *sin couches at the door*. חַטָּאת chatat is grammatically feminine, but רֹבֵץ rovetz is masculine — a grammatical mismatch suggesting *sin* is being personified as a male figure (an animal, a demon) crouching at the doorway. The verb רָבַץ ravats is the verb for animals *lying-down-to-watch-or-ambush* (a wolf in Gen 49:9, predators in Ps 104:22). The picture is bestial-predatory, not abstract-moral.

Second, the word חַטָּאת chatat carries a double range: *sin* (the act) and *sin-offering* (the cultic remedy, the leading sense in Leviticus). At the door of Cain's life, either *sin is crouching* (about to overtake him) or *a sin-offering is crouching* (available, waiting to be brought). The double sense is productive ambiguity, not error.

Third, the second clause — *its longing is for you, but you shall rule over it* — is **verbatim parallel** to Gen 3:16, with pronouns swapped. In 3:16: 'your longing shall be for your husband, and he shall rule over you'. Here in 4:7: 'its longing is for you, and you shall rule over it'. Same noun *t'shuqah*, same verb *mashal*. The parallel forces a re-reading of 3:16 — if *sin's longing* in 4:7 is a hostile, predatory drive that must be mastered, then *the woman's longing* in 3:16 may also be contested-drive rather than tender affection. The verses comment on each other across the chapter break.

notes.official: **The unfinished sentence.** The Masoretic text leaves a gap: *Cain spoke to his brother Hevel* — and then nothing. What Cain said is not recorded. The verse continues with *and while they were in the field*. The Samaritan Pentateuch, the LXX, and several other ancient versions fill the gap with a clause like *'Let us go out to the field'* — likely an early scribal addition to smooth the syntax. The Masoretic gap is conspicuous: Cain's words are absent. Whatever passed between brothers in the field, the text refuses to record. Only the act is preserved: וַיָּקָם vayyaqam ('and he rose up'), וַיַּהַרְגֵהוּ vayyahargehu ('and he killed him'). The first homicide is described with the bare verb הָרַג harag, the same verb that will return six verses later in Lamech's escalating song.

notes.official:
**The second divine 'where' question.** In 3:9 YHWH-Elohim asked the human *ayekka* — 'where are you?'. Now YHWH asks Cain *ei hevel achikha* — 'where is Hevel your brother?'. The first question opened a chain of self-disclosure; this one opens a chain of denial. Cain answers with a lie (*I do not know*) and a rhetorical question (*am I my brother's keeper?*).

The verb in 'keeper' is שָׁמַר shamar — the same verb used of the human's mandate in 2:15 (*to work the garden and to keep it*) and of the cherubim's mandate in 3:24 (*to guard the way to the tree of life*). The keeping-vocabulary returns, now in the form of a denial. Cain refuses the relational structure the verb names. The chapter's most famous line is a rejection of a category the text takes as given.

notes.official:
*Demei achikha tzo'aqim* — **your brother's bloods cries out**. Two precise Hebrew features. דְּמֵי demei is the **plural** of דָּם dam — Hebrew uses plural blood for *shed* blood, blood as forensic evidence (Lev 17:4, Isa 33:15, Hab 2:8). The plural is a register of testimony. And the participle צֹעֲקִים tzo'aqim is itself **plural**, agreeing with the plural noun: the bloods *cry out*, multiple voices. The ground has not absorbed and silenced; it amplifies. The same adamah that received Cain's offering in v3 — now refused to give him produce in v12 — is here a testifying witness against him.

The verb צָעַק tza'aq is the cry of the oppressed (used of the Hebrews in Egypt, Ex 2:23; of the widow and orphan, Ex 22:22). The Genesis text positions Hevel's spilled blood in the same vocabulary register as the cry of the wronged-and-voiceless throughout the Torah. The shed blood is, in the text's grammar, an oppressed witness.

notes.official:
**The first human to receive the curse formula directly.** In 3:14 the serpent received *arur attah* ('cursed are you'). In 3:17 the *ground* received *arurah ha-adamah* ('cursed is the ground'). The human and the woman did not. Now in 4:11, Cain receives *arur attah* — the same formula given to the serpent. The line that began in chapter 3 with the serpent under direct curse now adds Cain to that category.

The preposition מִן min has range: separative ('cursed *away from* the ground' — exile) or causative ('cursed *by* the ground' — the ground is now agent against him). Both readings work; the Hebrew leaves both in play. The ground that bore Hevel's blood as testimony in v10 is now the curse-bearer or curse-source against Cain. The same adamah Cain was supposed to *work* (v2) has turned actively hostile.

Note the personification: *the ground which opened its mouth*. The adamah is given a mouth — not metaphorical here but quasi-mythic, with an active swallow-and-receive action. Genesis often imagines the ground as a quasi-living surface; here it has actively *taken* the blood from Cain's hand.

notes.official:
**The mandate withdrawn.** The verb עָבַד avad ('to work') is Cain's defining occupation (v2: *oved adamah*). YHWH does not forbid the work — Cain is told 'when you work the ground' — but the response of the ground is withdrawn: *it shall no longer give its strength to you*. The relation of work-to-yield is broken for him.

In its place: נָע וָנָד na va-nad. Two participles of restless motion. נָע na from נוּעַ 'to wander aimlessly'. נָד nad from נוּד 'to wander, flee'. The alliterative pair signals continuous, purposeless movement. In v16 this condition will fuse with the place-name נוֹד Nod ('Wandering') — the address becomes the condition. Cain is exiled from settled relation to the ground; the worker's mandate ends in his line.

notes.official:
**The triple ambiguity.** עָוֹן avon spans three senses: (1) the *act* of sin, (2) the *guilt* it carries, (3) the *punishment/consequence* of the sin. The lexicon does not separate them — one word holds all three. The verb נָשָׂא nasa is similarly multivalent: 'to bear, carry, lift' — and in theological register, 'to bear away, to forgive'.

Cain's cry reads three ways at once: (a) my *guilt* is too great to bear — remorse, (b) my *punishment* is too great to bear — complaint, (c) my *iniquity is too great to be lifted (i.e., forgiven)* — despair of mercy. Tradition has read each. KJV ('my punishment is greater than I can bear') chose (b). Some Jewish commentaries (Rashi) chose (a). The Augustinian tradition is sometimes drawn to (c). The Hebrew supports all three; the text refuses to disambiguate. Cain's anguish is grammatically as multivalent as his act.

i18n.de: Siehe, du hast mich heute vom Angesicht des Ackerbodens vertrieben, und vor deinem Angesicht werde ich verborgen sein; fliehend und unstet werde ich sein auf dem Land, und jeder, der mich findet, wird mich töten.
i18n.es: He aquí, me has echado hoy de la faz del suelo, y de tu faz seré ocultado; seré errante y vagabundo en la tierra, y cualquiera que me halle me matará.
i18n.fr: Voici, tu m'as chassé aujourd'hui de la face du sol, et de ta face je serai caché ; je serai errant et vagabond sur la terre, et quiconque me trouvera me tuera. »
i18n.ja: 見よ、あなたは今日、私を大地の面から追い出された。私はあなたの顔から隠され、地の上でさすらい、さまよう者となるでしょう。そして私を見いだす者は誰でも、私を殺すでしょう」。
i18n.ko: 보소서, 당신이 오늘 저를 땅의 표면에서 쫓아내시니, 제가 당신의 얼굴을 피하여 숨을 것이며; 저는 땅에서 떠돌며 방황하는 자가 될 것이고, 저를 찾는 자는 누구든지 저를 죽일 것입니다.
i18n.ru: Вот, Ты изгнал меня сегодня с лица земли, и от лица Твоего я буду сокрыт; и буду я скитальцем и бродягой на земле, и всякий, кто встретит меня, убьёт меня».
i18n.zh: 看哪，你今日把我从可耕之地之面赶出去，我必从你的面前隐藏；我在大地上必流离飘荡，凡找到我的，必杀我。」
i18n.zh-Hant: 看哪，祢今日將我從土壤的面前驅逐出去，我也必從祢的面前隱藏；我必在大地上流離飄蕩，凡遇見我的都將殺我。

notes.official: **Cain names four losses.** He is *driven from the face of the ground* (the *adamah* he worked, now barren to him, v12); *hidden from your face* (exile from the divine presence — *nistar*, the same concealment the human attempted in 3:8, now imposed rather than chosen); a *wanderer and fugitive*; and exposed — *whoever finds me will kill me*. That last clause quietly presupposes a populated world the narrative has not accounted for (the perennial "who else is there?" crux); the text is unbothered by it — its concern is the blood-vengeance Cain now dreads. These named losses are what the protective sign of v15 is given to answer.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ יְהוָ֗ה לָכֵן֙ כָּל־הֹרֵ֣ג קַ֔יִן שִׁבְעָתַ֖יִם יֻקָּ֑ם וַיָּ֨שֶׂם יְהוָ֤ה לְקַ֙יִן֙ א֔וֹת לְבִלְתִּ֥י הַכּוֹת־אֹת֖וֹ כָּל־מֹצְאֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: YHWH said to him, "Therefore — whoever kills Cain, he will be avenged sevenfold." And YHWH placed for Cain a sign, so that no one who found him would strike him.
i18n.he: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ יְהוָ֗ה לָכֵן֙ כָּל־הֹרֵ֣ג קַ֔יִן שִׁבְעָתַ֖יִם יֻקָּ֑ם וַיָּ֨שֶׂם יְהוָ֤ה לְקַ֙יִן֙ א֔וֹת לְבִלְתִּ֥י הַכּוֹת־אֹת֖וֹ כָּל־מֹצְאֽוֹ׃
i18n.de: YHWH sprach zu ihm: "Darum — wer Kajin tötet, an dem soll es siebenfach gerächt werden." Und YHWH setzte für Kajin ein Zeichen, damit niemand, der ihn fände, ihn erschlüge.
i18n.es: YHWH le dijo: «Por tanto—quien mate a Caín, será vengado siete veces». Y YHWH puso para Caín una señal, para que ninguno que lo hallase lo hiriese.
i18n.fr: YHWH lui dit : « Aussi — quiconque tuera Caïn, il en sera vengé sept fois. » Et YHWH plaça un signe sur Caïn, afin que quiconque le trouverait ne le frappât point.
i18n.ja: YHWHは彼に言った、「それゆえ——誰であれカインを殺す者は、七倍の復讐を受ける」。そしてYHWHはカインのために、彼を見いだす者が彼を打つことのないように、しるしを置いた。
i18n.ko: YHWH께서 그에게 말씀하셨다, "그러므로 — 누구든지 카인을 죽이는 자는, 일곱 배로 보복을 받을 것이다." 그리고 YHWH께서 카인에게 표징을 두어, 그를 찾는 자가 그를 치지 못하게 하셨다.
i18n.ru: И сказал ему YHWH: «За то всякому, кто убьёт Каина, отомстится всемеро». И положил YHWH Каину знамение, чтобы никто, встретив его, не поразил его.
i18n.zh: YHWH 对他说：「因此——凡杀该隐的，必受七倍的报。」YHWH 就给该隐立了一个标记，免得遇见他的人击杀他。
i18n.zh-Hant: YHWH 對他說：「因此—凡殺該隱的，必遭七倍的報應。」YHWH 給該隱立了一個標記，使凡遇見他的不傷害他。

notes.official:
**A protection, not a brand.** The conventional 'mark of Cain' has a long medieval afterlife, often imagined as a forehead-stamp visible to other humans. The Hebrew is more open. אוֹת ot is *sign* in the generic sense — covering the rainbow (9:13), circumcision (17:11), the Sabbath (Ex 31:13), and miraculous portents (Ex 4:8–9). The preposition is לְ l- ('for/to'), not עַל al ('on/upon'). The sign is *for* Cain, not *on* him. It could be carried, accompanied, or stationed near. The text refuses to specify.

The sevenfold-vengeance formula is the structural counterpart of the sign: an absolute disproportion-protection. The same numeral (7×) will return in v24 with Lamech multiplying it to 77× — but in Cain's case, it is *defensive* (the multiplier shields him from being killed). The formula is given by YHWH, not claimed by Cain.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֥צֵא קַ֖יִן מִלִּפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב בְּאֶֽרֶץ־נ֖וֹד קִדְמַת־עֵֽדֶן׃

i18n.en: Cain went out from the presence of YHWH, and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
i18n.he: וַיֵּ֥צֵא קַ֖יִן מִלִּפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב בְּאֶֽרֶץ־נ֖וֹד קִדְמַת־עֵֽדֶן׃
i18n.de: Kajin ging fort vom Angesicht YHWHs und ließ sich nieder im Land Nod, östlich von Eden.
i18n.es: Caín salió de la presencia de YHWH, y se estableció en la tierra de Nod, al oriente de Edén.
i18n.fr: Caïn sortit de la présence de YHWH, et s'établit au pays de Nod, à l'orient d'Éden.
i18n.ja: カインはYHWHの面前から出て行き、エデンの東、ノドの地に住みついた。
i18n.ko: 카인이 YHWH의 앞에서 나가서, 에덴 동쪽 놋 땅에 정착하였다.
i18n.ru: И вышел Каин от лица YHWH и поселился в земле Нод, к востоку от Эдена.
i18n.zh: 于是该隐从 YHWH 面前出去，住在伊甸东边挪得之地。
i18n.zh-Hant: 該隱從 YHWH 的面前出去，住在伊甸東邊的挪得之地。

notes.official:
**The condition becomes the address.** נוֹד Nod is morphologically identical to the participle נָד nad ('wandering') from v12. The land's name *is* Cain's punishment — 'the land of Wandering'. He is sentenced to wander and then settles in *Wandering*. The geography fuses with the verdict.

*East of Eden* — קִדְמַת־עֵדֶן qidmat-eden. The east-axis returns. In 3:24 the cherubim were placed at the *east* of the garden; now Cain settles further east still. The west-east axis tracks an exilic motion: humans began in Eden, were placed in the garden eastward (2:8), driven out east-ward (3:24), and now Cain has extended the eastward direction. The garden is irrecoverably to the west of every subsequent step. The chapter's geography is moral as well as spatial.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֤דַע קַ֙יִן֙ אֶת־אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַתַּ֖הַר וַתֵּ֣לֶד אֶת־חֲנ֑וֹךְ וַֽיְהִי֙ בֹּ֣נֶה עִ֔יר וַיִּקְרָא֙ שֵׁ֣ם הָעִ֔יר כְּשֵׁ֖ם בְּנ֥וֹ חֲנֽוֹךְ׃

i18n.en: Cain knew his wife, and she conceived and bore Hanokh. And he was building a city, and he called the name of the city after the name of his son — Hanokh.
i18n.he: וַיֵּ֤דַע קַ֙יִן֙ אֶת־אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַתַּ֖הַר וַתֵּ֣לֶד אֶת־חֲנ֑וֹךְ וַֽיְהִי֙ בֹּ֣נֶה עִ֔יר וַיִּקְרָא֙ שֵׁ֣ם הָעִ֔יר כְּשֵׁ֖ם בְּנ֥וֹ חֲנֽוֹךְ׃
i18n.de: Kajin erkannte seine Frau, und sie empfing und gebar Hanoch. Und er baute eine Stadt und nannte den Namen der Stadt nach dem Namen seines Sohnes — Hanoch.
i18n.es: Caín conoció a su mujer, y ella concibió y dio a luz a Henoc. Y él estaba construyendo una ciudad, y llamó el nombre de la ciudad según el nombre de su hijo—Henoc.
i18n.fr: Caïn connut sa femme, et elle conçut et enfanta Hénoch. Et il bâtissait une ville, et il appela le nom de la ville d'après le nom de son fils — Hénoch.
i18n.ja: カインはその妻を知り、彼女は身ごもってエノクを産んだ。彼は町を建てつつあり、その町の名を、息子の名にちなんでエノクと呼んだ。
i18n.ko: 카인이 자기 아내를 알았고, 그녀가 잉태하여 에녹을 낳았다. 그리고 그가 성을 짓고 있었는데, 자기 아들의 이름을 따서 그 성의 이름을 에녹이라 불렀다.
i18n.ru: И познал Каин жену свою, и она зачала и родила Еноха. И он строил город, и назвал имя города по имени сына своего—Енох.
i18n.zh: 该隐与他的妻子同房；她怀孕，生了以拿。该隐建造了一座城，就按他儿子的名给那城起名——以拿。
i18n.zh-Hant: 該隱認識了他的妻子，她懷孕生了以諾。他那時正在建一座城，便按他兒子的名為那城起名—以諾。

notes.official:
**The first city.** Cain — sentenced to wander — *builds a city*. The Hebrew is precise about the contradiction: בֹּנֶה עִיר boneh ir, a present-participle of habitual action ('he was building'). The verse does not present a finished city but an ongoing project. The city is named after Cain's son Hanokh (חֲנוֹךְ from חָנַךְ 'to dedicate, initiate'). The line that fled the worker-of-the-ground mandate begins urbanization — building, naming, fixing a place. The Cain line will further specialize in tent-dwelling, music, and metalwork (vv. 20–22). Civilization, in this telling, begins in the line of the exile.

Note that the wife arrives in the verse without introduction. The text is silent on her origin (a long-standing interpretive question — sister, separately-created human, an outside lineage). Genesis takes the population for granted at this point; the reader has only Cain, Hevel (now dead), Adam, and Chavvah explicitly on the page.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּוָּלֵ֤ד לַֽחֲנוֹךְ֙ אֶת־עִירָ֔ד וְעִירָ֕ד יָלַ֖ד אֶת־מְחֽוּיָאֵ֑ל וּמְחִיּיָאֵ֗ל יָלַד֙ אֶת־מְת֣וּשָׁאֵ֔ל וּמְתוּשָׁאֵ֖ל יָלַ֥ד אֶת־לָֽמֶךְ׃

i18n.en: To Hanokh was born Irad; and Irad fathered Mehuyael; and Mehuyael fathered Methushael; and Methushael fathered Lamech.
i18n.he: וַיִּוָּלֵ֤ד לַֽחֲנוֹךְ֙ אֶת־עִירָ֔ד וְעִירָ֕ד יָלַ֖ד אֶת־מְחֽוּיָאֵ֑ל וּמְחִיּיָאֵ֗ל יָלַד֙ אֶת־מְת֣וּשָׁאֵ֔ל וּמְתוּשָׁאֵ֖ל יָלַ֥ד אֶת־לָֽמֶךְ׃
i18n.de: Dem Hanoch wurde Irad geboren; und Irad zeugte Mehujael; und Mehujael zeugte Methuschael; und Methuschael zeugte Lemech.
i18n.es: A Henoc le nació Irad; e Irad engendró a Mehuyael; y Mehuyael engendró a Metushael; y Metushael engendró a Lamec.
i18n.fr: À Hénoch naquit Irad ; et Irad engendra Mehouyaël ; et Mehouyaël engendra Metoushaël ; et Metoushaël engendra Lémek.
i18n.ja: エノクにはイラデが生まれた。イラデはメフヤエルをもうけ、メフヤエルはメトシャエルをもうけ、メトシャエルはレメクをもうけた。
i18n.ko: 에녹에게서 이랏이 태어났다; 이랏은 므후야엘을 낳았고; 므후야엘은 므드사엘을 낳았으며; 므드사엘은 라멕을 낳았다.
i18n.ru: И у Еноха родился Ирад; и Ирад родил Мехуяэля; и Мехуяэль родил Метушаэля; и Метушаэль родил Лемеха.
i18n.zh: 以拿生了以拉；以拉生了米户雅利；米户雅利生了玛土撒利；玛土撒利生了拉麦。
i18n.zh-Hant: 以諾生了以拿；以拿生了米戶雅利；米戶雅利生了瑪土撒利；瑪土撒利生了拉麥。

notes.official: **A genealogy that shadows another.** The Cainite line here — Enoch, Irad, Mehujael, Methushael, Lamech — runs remarkably close to the Sethite line of chapter 5: the two share a skeleton (Cain/Kenan, Enoch/Enoch, Irad/Jared, Mehujael/Mahalalel, Methushael/Methuselah, and Lamech in both). The overlap in names and order is too dense for coincidence, and the standard reading takes the two as developments of a single antediluvian tradition — one list of long-lived pre-flood ancestors preserved in two branches (a pattern with a further analogue in the long-reigning kings of the Sumerian King List). Here the branch turns toward the city and the sword; in chapter 5 the other turns toward the one who "walked with the Elohim." The shared frame is what makes the divergence legible.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּֽקַּֽח־ל֥וֹ לֶ֖מֶךְ שְׁתֵּ֣י נָשִׁ֑ים שֵׁ֤ם הָֽאַחַת֙ עָדָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית צִלָּֽה׃

i18n.en: Lamech took for himself two wives: the name of the first was Adah, and the name of the second Tzillah.
i18n.he: וַיִּֽקַּֽח־ל֥וֹ לֶ֖מֶךְ שְׁתֵּ֣י נָשִׁ֑ים שֵׁ֤ם הָֽאַחַת֙ עָדָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית צִלָּֽה׃
i18n.de: Lemech nahm sich zwei Frauen: der Name der ersten war Ada, und der Name der zweiten Zilla.
i18n.es: Lamec tomó para sí dos mujeres: el nombre de la primera era Adá, y el nombre de la segunda Tzilá.
i18n.fr: Lémek prit pour lui deux femmes : le nom de la première était Ada, et le nom de la seconde Tsilla.
i18n.ja: レメクは自分のために二人の妻をめとった。第一の名はアダ、第二の名はツィラであった。
i18n.ko: 라멕이 자기를 위해 두 아내를 취하였으니: 첫째의 이름은 아다였고, 둘째의 이름은 칠라였다.
i18n.ru: И взял себе Лемех двух жён: имя первой—Ада, а имя второй—Цилла.
i18n.zh: 拉麦娶了两个妻子：一个名叫亚大，另一个名叫洗拉。
i18n.zh-Hant: 拉麥娶了兩個妻子：第一個名叫亞大，第二個名叫洗拉。

notes.official: *Two wives* — the first polygamy the narrative records, and it is set in the line of Cain. The text passes no explicit sentence, but the placement is pointed: Lamech, seventh from Adam in this line, is the figure whose boast (vv. 23–24) escalates Cain's vengeance from sevenfold to seventy-sevenfold. Adah and Tzillah are named because they matter to what follows — the three sons who found the arts of mobile and settled life (vv. 20–22).

paragraphs.text: וַתֵּ֥לֶד עָדָ֖ה אֶת־יָבָ֑ל ה֣וּא הָיָ֔ה אֲבִ֕י יֹשֵׁ֥ב אֹ֖הֶל וּמִקְנֶֽה׃

i18n.en: Adah bore Yaval; he was the ancestor of those who dwell in tents and have livestock.
i18n.he: וַתֵּ֥לֶד עָדָ֖ה אֶת־יָבָ֑ל ה֣וּא הָיָ֔ה אֲבִ֕י יֹשֵׁ֥ב אֹ֖הֶל וּמִקְנֶֽה׃
i18n.de: Ada gebar Jabal; er war der Stammvater derer, die in Zelten wohnen und Vieh besitzen.
i18n.es: Adá dio a luz a Yabal; él fue el antepasado de los que habitan en tiendas y tienen ganado.
i18n.fr: Ada enfanta Yabal ; il fut l'ancêtre de ceux qui habitent sous des tentes et possèdent du bétail.
i18n.ja: アダはヤバルを産んだ。彼は天幕に住み家畜を飼う者たちの祖となった。
i18n.ko: 아다가 야발을 낳았으니; 그는 천막에서 살며 가축을 치는 자들의 조상이었다.
i18n.ru: И родила Ада Ябала; он был предком тех, кто живёт в шатрах и имеет скот.
i18n.zh: 亚大生了雅八；他是住帐棚、牧牲畜之人的祖先。
i18n.zh-Hant: 亞大生了雅八；他是住帳棚、有牲畜之人的始祖。

notes.official: **The arts of civilization descend from the line of the exile.** The formula *avi X* — "father/ancestor of" those who live or work a certain way — is aetiological: Yaval is cast as the founder of tent-dwelling herding (mobile pastoralism), his brother Yuval of music (v21), and their half-brother Tuval-Cain of metallurgy (v22). Three foundational crafts, assigned to a single family. The placement is deliberate and double-edged. Culture's building blocks — the herd, the lyre, the forged blade — are traced not to the favoured line but to the descendants of Cain the wanderer, whose father had already "built a city" (v17). The narrative grants civilization its due and roots it, unsettlingly, in the cursed branch.

paragraphs.text: וְשֵׁ֥ם אָחִ֖יו יוּבָ֑ל ה֣וּא הָיָ֔ה אֲבִ֕י כָּל־תֹּפֵ֥שׂ כִּנּ֖וֹר וְעוּגָֽב׃

i18n.en: And his brother's name was Yuval; he was the ancestor of all who take up the lyre and the pipe.
i18n.he: וְשֵׁ֥ם אָחִ֖יו יוּבָ֑ל ה֣וּא הָיָ֔ה אֲבִ֕י כָּל־תֹּפֵ֥שׂ כִּנּ֖וֹר וְעוּגָֽב׃
i18n.de: Und der Name seines Bruders war Jubal; er war der Stammvater all derer, die Leier und Flöte ergreifen.
i18n.es: Y el nombre de su hermano era Yubal; él fue el antepasado de todos los que toman la lira y la flauta.
i18n.fr: Et le nom de son frère était Youbal ; il fut l'ancêtre de tous ceux qui prennent la lyre et la flûte.
i18n.ja: その弟の名はユバル。彼は竪琴と笛を取るすべての者たちの祖となった。
i18n.ko: 그의 아우의 이름은 유발이었으니; 그는 수금과 피리를 잡는 모든 자들의 조상이었다.
i18n.ru: А имя брата его—Юбал; он был предком всех, кто берёт лиру и свирель.
i18n.zh: 他兄弟的名字叫犹八；他是一切弹琴吹笛之人的祖先。
i18n.zh-Hant: 他兄弟名叫猶八；他是一切彈琴吹笛之人的始祖。

notes.official: **The Cain line specializes.** Three crafts emerge in three sons across two wives: Yaval — pastoralism (tent-dwelling and livestock); Yuval — music (string and wind instruments); Tuval-Cain — metallurgy (bronze and iron working). The triad represents the foundational technical-civilizational arts of the ANE world. The line that began with a fratricide and an exile produces the first specialists of urban life. Whether the chapter is reading this as triumphal advance or as the moral ambiguity of skilled labor downstream of violence — the text refuses to comment. The achievement and the lineage are placed side by side without judgment.

notes.official:
**The first poem in the Hebrew Bible.** The structure is poetic — parallel lines, formal address, chiastic patterning. Lamech opens with a vocative doubling (his wives' names, then *wives of Lamech*), then states the matched pair: *a man for my wounding, a child for my bruising*. The Hebrew is tightly compressed: אִישׁ הָרַגְתִּי לְפִצְעִי וְיֶלֶד לְחַבֻּרָתִי — a man I have killed for my pesa, a child for my chabburah.

The verbal structure is parallelistic, as is the verb tense: הָרַגְתִּי haragti ('I have killed' or 'I would kill' — perfect tense with declarative force). The grammar is itself a boast: *I killed* a man for a wound, *I killed* a child for a bruise. The verse can be read as past-tense brag or as conditional threat ('I would kill anyone'); both are within the Hebrew's range. Either way, the line of Cain has moved from one fratricide to a poetic celebration of disproportionate vengeance.

notes.official:
**The multiplier escalates.** YHWH placed a sevenfold-vengeance protection on Cain in v15 — a defensive shield. Lamech inverts the formula's direction: he takes the same numeral structure and uses it to claim his own offensive vengeance-multiplier. Where Cain's was given (a divine ot), Lamech's is self-arrogated (a song). Where Cain's was protective (against anyone who would strike him), Lamech's is anticipatory (against anyone who might offend him).

The shift from 7× to 77× is the chapter's most compressed moral commentary. It is also the structural inverse of Yeshua's reply to Peter in Matthew 18:22 ('not seven times, but seventy-and-seven times' — the same numeral, but for *forgiveness* rather than *vengeance*). The numerical echo across canon is intentional in the receiving tradition; the original verse stands alone, in the line of Cain, naming the multiplication of violence.

notes.official:
**Two transitions in a single verse.**

First, the human's name shifts. Throughout chapters 2–4 he has been הָאָדָם ha-adam — 'the human', the article holding him as category-noun. Here in 4:25 the article drops: וַיֵּדַע אָדָם vayyeda adam — 'Adam knew'. The proper-name reading takes over. From this verse forward in Genesis, *Adam* will function as a personal name. The category-noun has become a person.

Second, the divine-reference vocabulary shifts. In 4:1 Chavvah named Cain with reference to *YHWH* (the personal name). Now in 4:25 she names Shet with reference to *Elohim* (the class/category name). The shift may be a P/J source seam, or it may register Chavvah's own changed relation to the divine after the loss of Hevel — from intimate personal-name to formal class-name. The text neither explains nor resolves the shift.

*Shet* (שֵׁת) is given the etymology immediately: שָׁת־לִי אֱלֹהִים shat-li Elohim — 'the Elohim has appointed/placed for me'. Same root, simple wordplay. The naming closes the chapter's family arc: Cain disinherited from the ground, Hevel killed, Shet appointed in his place. The Shet line will carry forward — and v26 will declare that the *calling on the name of YHWH* begins in it.

notes.official:
**The chapter closes on an origin.** The verb הוּחַל huchal is *hophal* (passive of the hiphil) of חָלַל — 'it was begun', impersonal passive. Hebrew here has no explicit subject — the conventional 'then men began' (KJV, NRSV) supplies one to smooth the English. The Hebrew leaves the subject open: 'then it was begun to be called on the name of YHWH'. Some *practice* of name-calling started in this generation. Whether it was cultic invocation, public utterance, formal worship, or something less defined — the text refuses to specify.

The verse is the chapter's terminal contrast. The Cain line ended in metallurgy and the vengeance-song (v22–24). The Shet line ends with a son named *Enosh* ('mortal, frail human') and the inauguration of name-calling on YHWH. Both genealogies have produced foundational human practices. The chapter places them side by side, naming the one that will become Israel's worship — but not before naming the other one with full lineage and craft-specialty.
